ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is a chord of $\odot O$ (AB is not a diameter). Taking point A as the center and the length of AB as the radius, an arc is drawn to intersect $\odot O$ at point C. Connect AC, BC, OB, and OC. If $\angle ABC=65^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given, we can derive: AB=AC, \\
$\because$ $\angle$ABC=65°, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ACB=65°, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$A=50°, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BOC=\boxed{100^\circ}

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is circle O, point A is located above the circle, point B is at the lower left of the circle, and point C is at the lower right of the circle; AB, AC, and BC are all connected to form triangle ABC, O is inside the circle, and OB and OC are radii from the center O connected to B and C. The figure also shows an auxiliary arc drawn with A as the center passing through the lower region and intersecting the circle at C. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem, draw an arc with A as the center and AB as the radius, and it intersects the circle at C, so AC = AB. Therefore triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, with base BC, and the base angles are equal. It is known that ∠ABC = 65°, so ∠ACB = 65°. Thus ∠BAC = 180° - 65° - 65° = 50°. ∠BAC is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is arc BC; ∠BOC is the central angle subtending the same arc BC, so ∠BOC = 2∠BAC = 100°.
